finding.claim: Caller identity is taken from the client-supplied X-Session-User-Verified header with no signature, token, session, or trusted-proxy verification, so any client can impersonate a user holding grants and delete or rename files.
finding.source: views.py:11 request.headers.get("X-Session-User-Verified") (attacker-controlled HTTP header on every route)
finding.sink: views.py:18 del STORE[fid] (delete, gated by views.py:17 ensure_allowed) and views.py:27 f["name"] = request.json["name"] (rename, gated by views.py:25 is_allowed)

trace.note: before_request stores the unverified header value in g.user
is_allowed checks action in grants.get(user, []) using the spoofed user
abort(403) only when the spoofed user lacks the grant
name is overwritten with attacker-supplied JSON

finding.guards_checked: Grant check at acl.py:5 and its 403 enforcement (acl.py:10, views.py:26) are used and correct for object-level authz, but they consume the spoofed identity. Missing header yields None, which is denied, so anonymous access is safe. No verification of the header exists anywhere in the repo. Exploitability depends on deployment: if a proxy strips and resets this header, the bug does not apply; the repo does not show that config, so this must be confirmed.

verdict.guard_found: acl.py:4-5 is_allowed and acl.py:8-10 ensure_allowed (abort(403)) are real and correctly enforced, and views.py:25-26 checks is_allowed's result, but all three consume g.user, which views.py:11 sets straight from the client-supplied X-Session-User-Verified header. No signature, session, or header verification exists in the repo. The only possible blocker is an upstream proxy that strips and resets the header, which is not in the repo.
verdict.reason: Every trace line matches: views.py:11 copies the unverified header into g.user, and views.py:17 and views.py:25 authorize against that value via acl.py:5 and acl.py:10, so any client sending a known username with a grant can delete (views.py:18) or rename (views.py:27) files. The finding holds for this code as shown; if a deployed proxy overwrites this header, the exposure would not exist, and that config is outside the repo.
